gaps.title: Miranda v. Arizona
gaps.claim: At issue was whether the Miranda warnings were actually compelled by the Constitution, or were rather merely measures enacted as a matter of judicial policy.

gaps.title: Rusik
gaps.claim: His talent for sniffing out poached fish soon found him taking over the job of the police's canine team member. Rusik died in the line of duty in June 2003, when he was hit by a car during an inspection, immediately after searching a bus. He had apparently found smuggled sturgeon in the same car some time before, according to personnel at the police checkpoint.

gaps.title: Terry v. Ohio
gaps.claim: The rationale behind the Supreme Court decision revolves around the notion that, as the opinion argues, "the exclusionary rule has its limitations." According to the court, the meaning of the rule is to protect persons from unreasonable searches and seizures aimed at gathering evidence, not searches and seizures for other purposes (like prevention of crime or personal protection of police officers).

gaps.title: Terry v. Ohio
gaps.claim: However, in Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial District Court of Nevada, , the court held that neither of these remarks was controlling in a situation in which a state law required a detained person to identify himself.

gaps.title: Terry v. Ohio

gaps.title: Stop-and-frisk in New York City
gaps.claim: Giuliani (mayor 1994-2001) and Bratton presided over an expansion of the New York police department and a crackdown on low-level crimes, including fare evasion, public drinking, public urination, graffiti artists, and "squeegee men".

gaps.title: Implied consent
gaps.claim: For a handheld field breath tester to be used as evidential breath testing, the device must be properly certified and calibrated, evidential procedures must be followed, and it may be necessary to administer an "implied consent" warning to the suspect prior to testing.

gaps.title: Drunk driving
gaps.claim: In many jurisdictions, police officers can conduct field tests of suspects to look for signs of intoxication. There have been cases in Canada where officers have come upon a suspect who is unconscious after a crash and officers have taken a blood sample.

gaps.title: Warrant (law)
gaps.claim: The Parliament of Great Britain passed the Revenue Act 1767 (7 Geo. 3. c. 46) which reaffirmed the legality of writs of assistance, or general search warrants, and gave customs officials broad powers to search houses and businesses for smuggled goods. This law was one of the key acts of Great Britain which led to the American Revolution,

gaps.title: Warrant (law)
gaps.claim: The person being investigated, arrested, or having their property seized, pursuant to a warrant is given a copy of the warrant at the time of its execution.

gaps.title: Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution
gaps.claim: The amendment has also been used by defendants and witnesses in criminal cases involving the American Mafia.

gaps.title: Right to silence
gaps.claim: If you do wish to say anything, what you say may be given in evidence.
